title: Do Simulated Users Push Back Like Real Users? Correctness vs. Stance
abstract: arXiv:2611.28024v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: LLM-simulated users stand in for people in multi-turn evaluations, on the assumption that they react to what the assistant says. We test this for pushback. From WildChat, we take conversations in which the assistant explicitly challenges or endorses a position the user stated, and compare the real next user turn with simulated turns from the same prefix. Among users who replied, real users push back more after a challenge than after an endorsement (20.5% vs. 8.2%); a GPT-based simulator does not (27.1% vs. 27.1%): stance gap D = -0.12 [-0.17, -0.08]. After a challenge the simulator instead often re-states or re-interprets its request ("I meant ..."); about half of these turns are disguised insistence, which puts D between -0.08 and -0.05. What drives the simulator's disputing is whether the assistant's position is judged correct (21% vs. 49% after challenges; 16% vs. 58% after endorsements), while real users change little (19% vs. 24%;

translated_title: 模拟用户会像真实用户一样提出反驳吗？正确性对比立场
translated_abstract: LLM模拟用户在多轮评估中代替真人，其前提假设是它们会对助手的发言作出反应。我们针对“反驳”行为对这一假设进行了检验。我们从WildChat中选取助手明确质疑或认同用户所述立场的对话，并将真实的下一轮用户回复与相同前缀下模拟出的回复进行比较。在作出回复的用户中，真实用户在被质疑后的反驳比例高于被认同后的比例（20.5% vs. 8.2%）；而基于GPT的模拟器则并非如此（27.1% vs. 27.1%）：立场差距 D = -0.12 [-0.17, -0.08]。在被质疑后，模拟器往往转而重述或重新解释自己的请求（“我的意思是……”）；这类回复中约有一半属于变相的坚持，这使得D值介于-0.08与-0.05之间。驱动模拟器争辩的因素是助手的立场是否被判定为正确（被质疑后：21% vs. 49%；被认同后：16% vs. 58%），而真实用户的变化不大（19% vs. 24%; …）
tldr: 研究发现LLM模拟用户的反驳行为与真实用户存在系统性差异：真实用户更多是因为自身立场受到质疑而反驳，而模拟用户是否反驳取决于其对助手观点正确性的判断，即模拟器关注“对错”而非“立场”。
en_tdlr: LLM-simulated users push back based on whether they judge the assistant's position to be correct, whereas real users push back more when their own stance is challenged, revealing a fundamental correctness-vs-stance gap in simulated user behavior.
